verdicts.factCheck: The MegaETH L1 portal cap still holds today. eth_call of depositTransaction(address,uint256,uint64,bool,bytes) (selector 0xe9e05c42, keccak computed locally) on 0x7f82f57F0Dd546519324392e408b01fcC7D709e8 through https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com at latest on 2026-11-28 returns 0x for a gas limit of 1,000,000 and reverts with 'L2 message gas must not exceed 1 million' for 1,000,001. The dual gas model spec fetched today states that a 0 to nonzero SSTORE costs SSTORE_STORAGE_GAS_BASE times (multiplier minus 1), that multiplier is bucket capacity divided by MIN_BUCKET_SIZE from the parent block, that the bucket id is computed from contract address and slot key, and that only system originated transactions are exempt. The census was reproduced for one row: eth_getLogs on https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc for pool 0x56fe79f5...f844 gives the PositionManager 0x9ae0921e... full range position (ticks -887272 and 887272, salt 1, liquidity 1e12). Its position slot read with eth_getStorageAt holds liquidity 1,000,000,000,000 and zero in both fee growth last slots, while feeGrowthGlobal minus both tick outside values is 274,673,368,775,357,439,505,978,916,724 for currency0 and 1.209e41 for currency1, so its next update writes two new nonzero slots. The counts in out/l1332-positions.json recompute as stated: 138 live rows, all with slot liquidity equal to the log sum, 38 needing a new slot in 17 of 102 pools, 30 needing two, 21 owned by 0x9ae0921e..., 15 by 0x5f16b71c... and 2 by 0xdc41ab84.... The census script cycles/039/high-throughput.work/scripts/l1332_positions.py uses the storage layout the source defines. The claim that none of the 38 sits in the eight pools with the most liquidity was not checked.
verdicts.codeCheck: PoolManager.modifyLiquidity passes owner msg.sender (src/PoolManager.sol:161) and emits ModifyLiquidity with msg.sender and the salt (src/PoolManager.sol:175), so the log identifies the position. Pool.State puts ticks at offset 4 and positions at offset 6 (src/libraries/Pool.sol:83-91), TickInfo keeps the outside values at offsets 1 and 2 (src/libraries/Pool.sol:68-77), the pools mapping sits at slot 6 (src/libraries/StateLibrary.sol:11), the position key packs owner, ticks and salt into 58 bytes (src/libraries/Position.sol:47-60) and the tick sits at bit 160 of slot0 (src/types/Slot0.sol:36-49). Position.update writes both fee growth last values unconditionally after the fee computation (src/libraries/Position.sol:99-100), and getFeeGrowthInside uses the three branch rule the script reproduces (src/libraries/Pool.sol:488-511). Removal to zero does not delete the position struct, so the write happens on the removal itself. take and mint (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297 and 322-328) let the remover choose the recipient, so those first writes can be avoided as the finding says.
verdicts.corrections: The scale in SCHEMA.md puts a freeze that needs a sequencer at high, but the freeze here comes from the sequencer refusing the provider; the bucket growth only closes the L1 escape for positions holding about 17,000 dollars in total, so medium as recorded in the ledger is kept. The statement about the eight largest pools is unverified.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Lead L-1340: can block 0xde6 of the compiled PoolManager (the delta read of clear) run its out-of-line CALLDATALOAD path for calldata shorter than 68 bytes?
clearedSpotChecks.note: A linear decode of cycles/023/high-throughput.work/pm143.bin (24,009 bytes, sha256 288b97729c9e4f34) shows the dispatcher at 0xe6 sending 0x80f0b44c to 0xd87, a CALLVALUE check, then SLT(calldatasize minus 4, 0x40) jumping to the revert at 0x330, the address check call at 0x2d3f returning to 0xdbe, the unlock TLOAD, and fall through to 0xde6, which is not a JUMPDEST. PUSH2 0x0dbe occurs only at 0xdb7. CALLDATALOAD(0x24) at 0xe0f is therefore reached only with calldata of at least 68 bytes. My own eth_call on https://rpc1.monad.xyz with 4 bytes of clear calldata reverted with empty data on 2026-11-28, which fills the gap the research left at 4 bytes; 36 and 100 bytes were rate limited.
